scope: Original51 figure 29 only; source prose belongs to D269.

sourcecrop.resampling: nearest; no enhancement or inferred ink

figure.layout: Left subdivision: six separate LC circuits, two rows by three columns. Right subdivision: one spring/mass state aligned with each row. No surrounding frame or grid.
figure.commonCircuitTopology: Rectangular closed loop with top and bottom horizontal solid wires; two thick horizontal capacitor plates interrupt the left vertical leg; four broad right-facing coil lobes form the right leg. The plate gap is not shorted. No switches, connection arrows, extra circuit branches or row-to-row wires.

caption.boundary: Caption is part of figure. Surrounding paragraph ending above first heading and printed page number 41 below/right are not figure content.

figure.contourAndBoundary: Original is binary-looking ink on white with ragged scan contours, thick plates, coarse round masses and nonuniform wire/coil strokes. Figure extremities, both headings, both equilibrium labels, both subdivision marks and complete caption lie inside the recorded sourcecrop; no paragraph or printed page number enters it. A few isolated specks outside instructional strokes belong to source scan noise.

limitations: A two-times nearest-neighbor crop enlarges existing pixels only. It does not recover unreadable glyphs.
M-like subscripts and a-shaped/b-like subdivision glyphs do not establish encoded Latin versus Cyrillic identities. Compare visible shape and placement, not Unicode identity.
At full charge, the outermost tiny repeated signs can merge visually with labels or plate contours; polarity and repeated-sign rows are definite, exact tiny-sign multiplicity is not asserted.
Lower spring small glyph/subscript and overlapping vertical marks are low-resolution. Preserve their visible strokes, two levels and downward head shapes without inventing a fully decoded formula.
Source prose above figure was not transcribed or assessed; D269 remains separate.
